facts.raw_span: A 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history
presented with a 3-month history of progressively worsening occipital headache
exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
bilateral past-pointing and an intention tremor
a 6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
extending craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale

aliases: Neuroma of the Eighth Cranial Nerve
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle, are consistent with an acoustic neuroma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a lobulated mass with multiloculated cystic areas and enhancing solid components, are consistent with a meningioma.

aliases: Neuroma of the Fifth Cranial Nerve
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with extension into the left infratemporal fossa, are consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a lobulated mass with multiloculated cystic areas and enhancing solid components, are consistent with a chordoma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a lobulated mass with multiloculated cystic areas and nonenhancing components, are consistent with an epidermoid cyst.
The patient's imaging findings, including a lobulated mass with multiloculated cystic areas and nonenhancing components, are consistent with an arachnoid cyst.

The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle with extension into the left infratemporal fossa, are consistent with a cranial nerve sheath tumor.
The patient's imaging findings, including a lobulated mass with multiloculated cystic areas and enhancing solid components, are consistent with a hemangioma.

rationales.F04: Bilateral past-pointing and intention tremor suggest cerebellar involvement, which is more typical of C01, C03, and C07.
rationales.F05: A large lobulated mass at the cerebellopontine angle is highly suggestive of a tumor, which could be C01, C02, C03, C04, C05, C06, C07, or C08.
rationales.F07: Multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas are more typical of epidermoid cysts (C05) or arachnoid cysts (C06).
rationales.F08: T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components are more typical of tumors such as C01, C02, C03, C04, or C07.
rationales.F09: Hemorrhagic foci are more typical of hemangiomas (C08).
rationales.F10: Compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem is highly suggestive of a tumor, which could be C01, C02, C03, C04, C05, C06, C07, or C08.
rationales.F11: Dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles is highly suggestive of a tumor, which could be C01, C02, C03, C04, C05, C06, C07, or C08.
rationales.F12: Smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale are more typical of chordomas (C04).

corrections.why: smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale is not typical for Acoustic Neuroma
